Imagine 50,000 people trying to escape a stadium. Running faster could actually slow everyone down.
Everyone wants to get out first. So they rush toward the same exit.
But when too many people compete for the same space, a bottleneck forms.
The harder they try to move, the less room everyone has.
Now watch what happens when the same crowd moves more steadily.
Under these conditions, the crowd moving more steadily can actually get out faster.
Scientists call this the faster-is-slower effect.
